page.layout: One page of text, single column, no margin notes. Inline italic references follow some paragraphs on the same line. Catchword at lower right.

main_text.p: Partium autem dissecandarum methodum, structuram & usus explicandos Anatomice priuatim sibi delegit.
Quatenus vero procreatur Homo, non Medico, sed Philosopho subijcitur: nosq; eadem physica, non didascalica medica esse iudicamus. Cl.Zuingero.
Ideoq; ubi Philosophus Naturalis definit, ibi Me-dicum incipere, rectissimè dictum.
Quandoquidem vero propter ægrotos Medicina & nunc & primum quoq; quæsita & inuenta fuerit, Pathologia summè necessaria exstitit. Hippocrat. lib. de veteri medicina: Galen. de artis constit.
Affectus vox tria præter naturam, Morbum, Causas, & Symptomata innuit.
Sæpe tamen pro Morbis habentur, quæ tantummodo sunt πάθη dicenda.
Morbus enim est διάθεσις præter naturā, à qua primum læditur actio. 2. de facult. natural. 1. de san. tuend. & Methodi, & alibi.
Morborum etiam proprie dictorum tria summa genera non immerito constituuntur, Similares, Organici, & Communes.
Omnis quoq; Morbus Vicus λόγῳ Hippocrati, recte ἐπιλέγει[?] τινὰ ἔχει. Libro de Fract. 3.

page.notes: Top numeral read as XXIIX. with possible colon. Greek in XXXVI is partly unclear; the middle word is marked [?]. The first letter of διάθεσις is a stylised initial; it is transcribed as printed. Printed long s in "diffecandarum", "fibi", "fumme", "exiftit" and "neceffaria" is given as plain s. "facut" in the citation for XXXIV is probably "facult." and is marked as uncertain. No page number or running head is printed.
